normalization.overview: NeuralNine reports that task-tuned 2B and 4B Qwen classifiers outperform a GPT-6 Luna baseline on one Shopify classification test, not across general intelligence.
normalization.whyItMatters: Task specialization and evaluation design matter more than the model leaderboard headline.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Choose models by the cost and accuracy of accepted work. A specialized classifier can beat a general-purpose pipeline for a narrowly defined job.

claims.assessment: On a 1,000-item Shopify test, the creator reports GPT-6 Luna 68.2%, tuned Qwen3.5-2B 69.8%, and tuned Qwen3.5-4B 73.0%.
claims.limits: No independent replication or paired per-item predictions. Small differences may not be reliable.

claims.proposition: Train/test examples are selected from named Shopify splits
claims.assessment: Creator code derives eligible labels from the full training split before selecting 5,000 training examples (random_state=42). It filters test items to labels found in that full split, then samples 1,000 evaluation examples. The selected 5,000 training examples are not guaranteed to contain every evaluated label.
claims.limits: Not every evaluated label is guaranteed to appear in the 5,000 sampled training examples; the full split defines the eligible labels. Original dataset revision, near-duplicate/product-family overlap, and distribution shifts were not audited.

claims.proposition: Prompts differ between tuned and untuned model pipelines
claims.assessment: Code supplies the candidate category list to Luna and untuned Qwen, but not to tuned Qwen adapters.
claims.limits: Cannot isolate the effect of fine-tuning alone under changed prompt conditions.

claims.proposition: Qwen decoding is specified but Luna defaults are not
claims.assessment: Qwen script uses do_sample=False, enable_thinking=False and max_new_tokens=40; Luna uses Responses API with no explicit effort/decoding pin.
claims.limits: API model revisions and the inference conditions were not pinned or independently repeated.

claims.proposition: Total cost or capability superiority has not been demonstrated
claims.assessment: A narrow classifier result is not a general model ranking or cost-per-accepted-job calculation.
claims.limits: No published training charges, matched inference accounting, latency/throughput, or exception costs.

claims.assessment: Crusoe sponsorship is disclosed by the creator in description and within the video.
claims.limits: The sponsorship is contextual provenance, not proof the benchmark outcome is incorrect.

relationships.reason: Reader #69 explains why price and total cost of an accepted job are different measures. It is a conceptual editorial companion, not validation of the reported classification percentages.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Right Model Is the One Your Eval Can Defend
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: The SharePlane playbook specifies representative task samples, comparative model baselines, trace-level failure analysis, latency, operating cost and retest triggers. It provides the missing evaluation discipline for interpreting this narrow Shopify result; it does not independently reproduce NeuralNine's scores.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Best AI System Should Need Less AI Tomorrow
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: The inference retirement thesis extends task specialization into system design: preserve validated repeatable work in deterministic machinery and reserve expensive reasoning for uncertainty. This is an operational extension of the Reader's argument, not evidence that the fine-tuned classifiers will generalize.

normalization.relationshipDisposition: Reader #69 is the sole related Reader, providing the full cost-of-completion lens; the separately labeled SharePlane Works develop evaluation discipline and inference architecture.
